result.summary: VERDICT: PASS (round 1). The blocker B1 and the three small findings F1, F3 and F6 are fixed, and I verified each one with my own runs (below). The regression run shows nothing weakened, and I found no new defect above INFO. Q7, Q10, Q11 and R2 pass; Q8, Q9 and R3 still do not apply (no shop data, no SQL, no customer photos). F2, F4, F5, F7 and F8 are still open, as ORCH ruled (accepted residual risks); I re-observed each one unchanged. My verdict is not final on its own: the owner confirms the merge (R1). Node ran under the private 22.21.1 copy first in PATH; the permission system did not refuse anything. WHAT I REVIEWED. Against my round-0 baseline exactly 5 files differ (shasum -c: 5 differ, 20 identical): tools/src/pixel-office/main.js, server.js, state-dir.js, journal.js and tools/README.md; their sha256 (first 12 hex) equal BACKEND-DEV's report (journal 03bb65e03f7c, main fb2762d4deea, server a82651f3e6df, state-dir 52436cb76382, README f7bc2ddc7e6a). hook.sh, hook.js, protocol.js, config.js, public/* and .claude/settings.json are unchanged. I read the four modules and the README in full. All 25 reviewed files have the same sha256 at the end of my re-check as at its start (nobody edited code meanwhile). prettier --check on the 4 modules and the README: clean; eslint --max-warnings 0 on src/pixel-office: exit 0; no eslint-disable / prettier-ignore / skip markers in the changed code. ITEMS ASSESSED - Q7 secrets by reference only: PASS. The new code reads and writes the secret only through a descriptor it checked; no secret in the changed code (no 40+ character token, no console.* in the server modules, error messages show paths and OS codes, never content: the short-secret case still prints only the path); README has no token and only three links (http://127.0.0.1:4780/ and the two code.claude.com pages); repo-wide grep for a secret word followed by 32+ characters is empty; all 12 grep -F strings of design 9.4 are in README. - Q8: NOT APPLICABLE (no shop data). Q9: NOT APPLICABLE (no SQL). R3: NOT APPLICABLE (no customer photos). - Q10 (realistic failures never crash anything; hooks never break or slow a session): PASS. B1 is closed (below); no other crash found: 43,200 fuzzed requests, 0 responses of 5xx, empty stderr; journal unwritable/unreadable/a directory/a link/a FIFO, corrupt lines, truncation, deleted state dir, floods, 3,000 idle connections, fd exhaustion, 800 parallel appends: all as in round 0 or better. The hook is unchanged and its whole matrix gives the same results as round 0 (always exit 0, silent, 1.55 s worst). - Q11 (server reachable only from the owner's computer): PASS, unchanged. server.listen(requestedPort, HOST) with HOST 127.0.0.1 (server.js:407); the 109 checks of t1 (17 foreign Host forms 403, no Access-Control-* on 17 response kinds, signed POST with wrong Host 403) and the real Chrome run (14 cross-origin attempts, 0 readable; rebinding Host evil.test: got 403) give the same results as round 0. - R2 (only real hook events): PASS, unchanged. The write path is byte-for-byte the same (protocol.js and processBody untouched); signatures, +-60 s window, has_source, unknown keys, sizes: t2 output is identical to round 0 line by line (diff of the normalised outputs is empty). B1 RE-VERIFIED (closed). Fix in main.js:296-317: before main() runs, an 'error' listener on process.stdout and process.stderr (:303-305). Because F1 removed the long-name trigger, I used three other warning triggers in every scenario: a corrupt journal line, a journal at mode 0000 (read failure), a journal at mode 0444 plus a signed POST (write failure). - My round-0 scripts: node t16-epipe.mjs -> "reader of stderr gone ... status=200 server alive=true" and "reader of stdout+stderr gone ... status=200 server alive=true" (round 0: alive=false, exit 1 in both). node t16b-epipe.mjs -> "answered 404; server: still running; uncaught log: (none)" (round 0: 500, exit 1, uncaughtException EPIPE). Note for TEST-DESIGNER: t16b no longer exercises B1 (F1 removed its trigger) and, as its script never stops the server it started, it now hangs until the server is stopped (I stopped it by pid: SIGTERM, exit 0); use t16 or r1-b1.mjs. - r1-b1.mjs, 8 scenarios, each: corrupt line -> GET 200; unreadable journal -> GET 500 read_failed; unwritable journal -> signed POST 500 write_failed; repair -> POST 204; long name, /nope and /api/events/ -> 404; final GET /api/events?after=0&limit=0 -> 200; process alive; SIGTERM -> exit code 0. All 8 OK: stderr reader destroyed after the link line; stdout+stderr readers destroyed after the link line; stdout reader gone BEFORE the link line (destroyed at spawn; stderr kept and inspected: 3 warning lines only, no stack, no EPIPE, no "Unhandled 'error' event"); stderr reader gone at spawn; both gone at spawn; fd 1 closed (>&-); fd 2 closed (2>&-); both closed (>&- 2>&-). - The literal shell repro of round 0 (main.js 2>&1 | head -n 1 > link, in the background): link line "Pixel Office: http://127.0.0.1:62341/" printed; long-name GET 404; GET after a corrupt journal line 200; again 200; server alive; SIGTERM stops it. Design E25 holds: with the stdout reader gone at start the server prints no raw stack (stderr text was only "Pixel Office: строка журнала 0 испорчена и пропущена"). - Adjacent failure: a stderr reader that is alive but never reads (the pipe fills with 20,000 warnings, 1.2 MB): the warning-producing GET answered 200 in 59 ms and the next GET in 1 ms, so the output channel cannot block the server either. F1 RE-VERIFIED (closed). server.js:58 STATIC_NAME = /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$/; server.js:66-72 NO_SUCH_FILE adds ENAMETOOLONG and ELOOP; readPublicFile :118 and handleStatic :189. r1-f1.mjs (19 checks OK): names of 10, 63, 64, 65, 100, 255, 256, 300, 4000, 8000 characters (.js), long .css/.html/no extension/dotted: all 404 {"error":"not_found"}; the server's stderr after all of them is empty (round 0: 500 and a stderr line with the repo path). With the real server code and a scratch public dir: an existing 64-character file is served (200, text/javascript), an existing 65-character file is 404; all 13 real files of public/ are served (200). Fuzz: node t12-fuzz.mjs and t12b-fuzz.mjs (2 x 21,600 requests, same generators and seeds as round 0): 0 responses of 5xx (round 0: 78), 0 stderr lines, server alive, journal unchanged by unsigned or garbage requests. F3 RE-VERIFIED (closed; no write and no chmod reaches a link target). Code: state-dir.js READ_FLAGS :28 (O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK), withSmallFile :113 (open, fstat regular file and at most 4096 bytes, close), readExistingSecret :214 (fchmodSync on the checked descriptor), writeSmallFile :262 (rmSync of the temp name, open "wx" 0600, fchmodSync(fd), writeAll, rename); journal.js APPEND_FLAGS :36 and READ_FLAGS :38 (O_NOFOLLOW), refresh :202 (lstat), readRegularText :100; server.js readPublicFile :118. A scan of every mutating fs call in tools/src/pixel-office (grep) leaves exactly one path-based chmod: state-dir.js:100 (the deliberate exception, judged below); every other chmod is fchmodSync on a descriptor; rmSync calls remove names, never targets. r1-f3.mjs (41 checks OK) and r1-f3b.mjs (the same 41 with a stricter test: link targets keep inode, size, ctime and mtime, so even a chmod that would not change the mode would show; targets of the first and the port case are already 0600): A (real main.js, links at start): write-secret as a link to a plain file -> exit 1 "...не читается или не годится (ELOOP)", target untouched; as a dangling link -> exit 1, the target is NOT created; events.jsonl as a link / dangling -> exit 1 "(ELOOP)", target untouched / not created; server-starts.jsonl as a link / dangling -> exit 1 "(ELOOP)", untouched / not created; port and node-path as links -> the server starts, both become regular 0600 files, targets untouched; port as a dangling link -> replaced, target not created; a FIFO in place of write-secret, events.jsonl or server-starts.jsonl -> exit 1 in 66-74 ms, no hang; a FIFO in place of port or node-path -> replaced, server starts. B (a link appears while the server runs): events.jsonl swapped for a link -> GET 500 read_failed and POST 500 write_failed, target untouched, back to 200 after the swap is undone; server-starts.jsonl swapped -> GET 500, then 200; write-secret swapped -> the hook-side readSecret returns null (the hook would post nothing), the server keeps its cached secret, the target is untouched. C (unit level, real modules): a link to a plain file / a dangling link / a link to a DIRECTORY planted at .tmp-: removed, never followed, targets and directory contents untouched; a directory at the temp name -> StateDirError E_STATE_WRITE, the previous file intact; a link at the target name port -> replaced by the rename, not followed; no *.tmp-* leftovers; readSecret on a link, dangling link, FIFO, directory, 5,000-byte file -> null each time in 2 ms total; ensureSecret with a FIFO -> typed error in 0 ms; journal.js against a link and a dangling link -> append, read, lineCount, recordStart, starts all refuse with ELOOP, target not created. D (public/, real createServer): a link to a file outside public/, a link to a directory (subpath), a dangling link, a directory named sub.js, a dotfile, a FIFO (no hang), and a real file name (style.css) turned into a link -> all 404, nothing leaked; app.js and index.html (with CSP) still 200. Also: a symlink in a PARENT component of the state path (like /tmp -> private/tmp) still works (only the leaf is checked, as designed): start OK, GET 200. OPINION ON THE DELIBERATE EXCEPTION (state-dir.js:98-107, chmodSync(dir, 0o700) after lstat says "directory, not a link, own uid"). Is it safe against a swap between lstat and chmod? Not in the strict sense, and I measured it: with chmodSync wrapped so that the entry is swapped for a link to a scratch file exactly between lstat and the chmod (r1-chmod-window.mjs), the path-based chmod went through the link and the scratch file went 0644 -> 0700. But it is safe in this threat model, and I accept the exception. (1) The swap needs write access to the PARENT directory of the state dir: for the default ~/.sai-pixel-office the parent is the home directory (mode drwxr-x---+, only the owner writes) and for a parent like /tmp the sticky bit stops others from replacing an entry that is not theirs; an entry that is already a link when lstat looks is refused (checked: E_STATE_DIR, victim untouched), and an entry of another uid is refused by state-dir.js:92 (code read; not testable on a one-user Mac). (2) A won race can only chmod a file or directory the same user owns (POSIX: chmod on another user's file fails with EPERM; not tested here, one-user machine), and it sets exactly 0700: it narrows, never widens, keeps the owner's read/write/execute (so it cannot take the execute bit away from the owner, the mechanism of the 2026-10-01 incident), and clears setuid/setgid/sticky. (3) The descriptor-based alternative would regress something real: opening a directory of mode 0000 for reading fails with EACCES (measured), so an fchmod could not repair it, while the path-based chmod repairs it (measured: 0000 -> 0700, as in my round-0 attack 7). Optional hardening, not required: open the directory with O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW, compare dev/ino from fstat with the lstat, fchmod(fd); fall back to chmodSync(path) after a second lstat only when the open fails with EACCES. Severity LOW to INFO; not a blocker. F6 RE-VERIFIED (closed). server.js:248 drainTimeoutSet (a WeakSet) and :254-261 answerTooLarge. node t9-listeners.mjs: "responses 413 on the same connection: 40 of 40; socket still open: true; server stderr: ''; server alive afterwards: true" (round 0: MaxListenersExceededWarning at the 11th); the same with 200 requests: 200 of 200, stderr empty. Idle-drop check, because setting the timeout once per socket could in theory lapse when Node resets the socket timeout between requests: A/B against scratch copies of the server (cur = the repo file byte for byte, old = round-0 behaviour, fix = re-arm every time with one listener, none = no timer of our own): a stalled oversized request is dropped after 6,007 / 6,003 / 6,005 ms (first request / second request on the same keep-alive connection / chunked third) for cur, 6,006 / 6,002 / 6,005 for old, 6,007 / 6,003 / 6,004 for fix, and 6,007 / 6,002 / 6,004 for none. So there is no weakening, and the drop is done by Node's own keepAliveTimeout, which starts when the 413 response finishes: the timer in answerTooLarge is redundant (INFO N3, harmless; my round-0 suggestion "arm once per socket" is thus not load-bearing either way). A slow drip (a byte every few seconds) was not measured: it would keep every idle timer from firing in all four variants alike, and would then be bounded by DRAIN_MAX (8 MiB) and Node's requestTimeout (300 s, the default I printed in round 0). NEW CODE: DEFECT HUNT (O_NOFOLLOW, fchmod, WeakSet, new flags). Permissions of the secret: a new secret is 0600 and 43 characters under umask 000 (fchmod on the creating descriptor); an existing 0644 secret is read and narrowed to 0600 through the same checked descriptor (same value returned); a link is refused; a short secret is left untouched with the old message; a failing narrowing fails closed (the start is refused: read from the code at state-dir.js:242-247, not testable as the file's owner). Atomic writes: port and node-path still go temp file -> rename (a planted link or leftover at the temp name is removed, not followed; the file is created exclusively with "wx"); the journal is still one write in O_APPEND mode: 800 parallel signed POSTs split over two servers sharing one state dir gave 800 intact, distinct, allow-listed lines and a regular 0600 file. No descriptor leak: 12,000 requests (static file, journal read with start records, 404 long name, signed append) and a 413 left the server at 38 descriptors, the same as before. O_NONBLOCK has no effect on regular files: full-journal reads of 100,000 and 300,000 lines took 215 and 669 ms (round 0: 223 and 656), append rate 15,164 lines/s (round 0: 15,233). The real npm command works: `npm run pixel-office -- --dir --port 0` printed the link, GET / 200, files 0600, SIGTERM stopped it. No new defect found above INFO.
